content: 1. Indinavir and Amikacin: Indinavir increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Indinavir and Amitriptyline: Indinavir increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Amobarbital and Indinavir: Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Indinavir and Apalutamide: Indinavir increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments may be required based on tolerability. 5. Indinavir and Apixaban: Indinavir increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Aprepitant and Indinavir: Aprepitant increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while indinavir also increases aprepitant levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Indinavir and Aripiprazole: Indinavir increases aripiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 8. Armodafinil and Indinavir: Armodafinil decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Artemether/Lumefantrine and Indinavir: Artemether/lumefantrine decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while indinavir increases artemether/lumefantrine levels. Caution and monitoring are required. 10. Atazanavir and Indinavir: Atazanavir increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. Indinavir and Atogepant: Indinavir increases atogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The recommended atogepant dose is 10 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 12. Atorvastatin and Indinavir: Atorvastatin increases indinavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Indinavir and Atovaquone: Indinavir decreases atovaquone levels through an unknown mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Azithromycin and Indinavir: Azithromycin increases indinavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are necessary. 15. Indinavir and Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Indinavir increases the levels of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are required. 16. Belzutifan and Indinavir: Belzutifan decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 17. Indinavir and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Indinavir increases benzhydrocodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 18. Berotralstat and Indinavir: Berotralstat increases indinavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Indinavir and Bexarotene: Indinavir increases bexarotene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. Indinavir and Bortezomib: Indinavir increases bortezomib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 21. Bosutinib and Indinavir: Bosutinib increases indinavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are necessary. 22. Indinavir and Brentuximab Vedotin: Indinavir increases brentuximab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients should be monitored for adverse reactions. 23. Indinavir and Brexpiprazole: Indinavir increases brexpiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The brexpiprazole dose should be halved when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Indinavir and Bromocriptine: Indinavir increases bromocriptine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Indinavir and Budesonide: Indinavir increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are necessary. 26. Indinavir and Buprenorphine: Indinavir increases buprenorphine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to toxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 27. Indinavir and Buspirone: Indinavir increases buspirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Butabarbital and Indinavir: Butabarbital decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 29. Indinavir and Cabazitaxel: Indinavir increases cabazitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to toxicity. Co-administration should be avoided. 30. Indinavir and Calcifediol: Indinavir affects vitamin D metabolism by inhibiting CYP3A4, potentially altering calcifediol levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 31. Indinavir and Cannabidiol: Indinavir increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of cannabidiol may be necessary. 32. Indinavir and Capmatinib: Indinavir increases capmatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Indinavir and Carbamazepine: Indinavir increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Plasma levels should be monitored. 34. Indinavir and Cariprazine: Indinavir increases cariprazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of cariprazine is required. 35. Cenobamate and Indinavir: Cenobamate decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 36. Indinavir and Chlordiazepoxide: Indinavir increases chlordiazepoxide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to toxicity. Alternatives should be considered. 37. Indinavir and Ciclesonide: Indinavir increases ciclesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Caution and monitoring are required. 38. Indinavir and Cilostazol: Indinavir increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 39. Indinavir and Cinacalcet: Indinavir increases cinacalcet levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Indinavir and Citalopram: Indinavir increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 41. Clarithromycin and Indinavir: Clarithromycin increases indinavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are required. 42. Indinavir and Clomipramine: Indinavir increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 43. Indinavir and Clonazepam: Indinavir increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to toxicity. Alternatives should be considered. 44. Indinavir and Clopidogrel: Indinavir decreases clopidogrel activation by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Indinavir and Clorazepate: Indinavir increases clorazepate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to toxicity. Alternatives should be considered. 46. Clotrimazole and Indinavir: Clotrimazole decreases indinavir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are necessary. 47. Indinavir and Clozapine: Indinavir increases clozapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Conivaptan and Indinavir: Conivaptan increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 49. Indinavir and Conjugated Estrogens: Indinavir increases conjugated estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are necessary. 50. Indinavir and Cortisone: Indinavir increases cortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Indinavir and Crizotinib: Indinavir increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while crizotinib increases indinavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are necessary. 52. Indinavir and Crofelemer: Crofelemer increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 53. Indinavir and Cyclophosphamide: Indinavir increases cyclophosphamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 54. Indinavir and Cyclosporine: Indinavir increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are required. 55. Dabrafenib and Indinavir: Dabrafenib decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 56. Danicopan and Indinavir: Danicopan increases indinavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Darifenacin and Indinavir: Darifenacin increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 58. Indinavir and Darolutamide: Indinavir increases darolutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 59. Darunavir and Indinavir: Darunavir increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 60. Dasatinib and Indinavir: Dasatinib increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 61. Deferasirox and Indinavir: Deferasirox decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 62. Indinavir and Deflazacort: Indinavir increases deflazacort levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 63. Indinavir and Desvenlafaxine: Indinavir increases desvenlafaxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to toxicity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 64. Indinavir and Dexamethasone: Indinavir increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are advised. 65. DHEA (Herbal) and Indinavir: DHEA increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 66. Indinavir and Diazepam: Indinavir increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to toxicity. Alternatives should be considered. 67. Indinavir and Diazoxide: Indinavir increases diazoxide effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are required. 68. Didanosine and Indinavir: Didanosine decreases indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Indinavir should be administered 1 hour before didanosine chewable tablets or powder. 69. Indinavir and Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Indinavir increases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring for adverse effects is recommended. 70. Indinavir and Digoxin: Indinavir increases digoxin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are necessary. 71. Diltiazem and Indinavir: Diltiazem increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 72. Indinavir and Dofetilide: Indinavir increases dofetilide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Alternatives should be considered. 73. Indinavir and Doravirine: Indinavir increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 74. Indinavir and Doxepin Cream: Indinavir increases doxepin cream levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 75. Indinavir and Doxorubicin: Indinavir increases doxorubicin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 76. Indinavir and Dronabinol: Indinavir increases dronabinol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 77. Dronedarone and Indinavir: Dronedarone increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 78. Indinavir and Duvelisib: Indinavir increases duvelisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 79. Indinavir and Efavirenz: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are required. 80. Elagolix and Indinavir: Elagolix increases indinavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1), while indinavir increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 81. Indinavir and Eletriptan: Indinavir increases eletriptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 82. Indinavir and Elvitegravir: Indinavir increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 83. Indinavir and Emtricitabine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are required. 84. Encorafenib and Indinavir: Encorafenib affects indinavir levels by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 85. Indinavir and Enfortumab Vedotin: Indinavir increases enfortumab vedotin toxicity by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 86. Indinavir and Erlotinib: Indinavir increases erlotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are necessary. 87. Erythromycin and Indinavir: Erythromycin increases indinavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are required. 88. Indinavir and Escitalopram: Indinavir increases escitalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 89. Eslcarbazepine Acetate and Indinavir: Eslcarbazepine decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 90. Indinavir and Estradiol: Indinavir increases estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are necessary. 91. Indinavir and Estrogens: Indinavir increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are required. 92. Indinavir and Eszopiclone: Indinavir increases eszopiclone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The starting dose of eszopiclone should be reduced to 1 mg/day. 93. Indinavir and Ethosuximide: Indinavir increases ethosuximide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 94. Indinavir and Etonogestrel: Indinavir increases etonogestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 95. Indinavir and Etoposide: Indinavir increases etoposide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Caution and monitoring are necessary. 96. Indinavir and Etravirine: Indinavir increases etravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 97. Indinavir and Exenatide: Indinavir decreases exenatide effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 98. Fedratinib and Indinavir: Fedratinib increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when indinavir is co-administered with other medications due to its significant impact on drug metabolism and transport.
